notes.meaning: People are warned against boasting about what they will do or experience in the future. No human being knows what a single day will produce, because tomorrow is entirely in God's hands. Making wise plans is fine, but presuming that tomorrow is guaranteed leads to pride and foolishness.

A person should let others speak well of him instead of praising himself. Boasting about one's own achievements reveals foolishness, self-love, and pride, and it only turns people away. Good deeds should speak for themselves, so that genuine honor comes naturally from strangers.

Heavy stones and heaps of sand are difficult physical burdens to carry. Even so, the unprovoked, unreasonable anger of a foolish person is much harder to bear. A fool lacks self-control, and his outbursts crush both himself and anyone standing in his way.

Sudden wrath can be cruel and anger can sweep through like an overwhelming flood. Yet jealousy is far more dangerous, because it festers quietly, schemes in secret, and refuses to be appeased. While a sudden burst of rage may quickly pass, bitter jealousy stays and seeks ruin.

A direct and honest correction is far better than hidden love that never shows itself in helpful actions. Real love must have the courage to speak up when a companion goes astray. Keeping quiet just to avoid tension is not kindness, because it leaves a friend trapped in harmful habits.

The painful words and reproofs of a true friend come from genuine faithfulness and a desire to help. In contrast, an enemy may shower someone with warm greetings and kisses, but those gestures conceal malice and deceit. We should welcome hard truths from those who care for our souls.

A person whose stomach is stuffed will turn away even from the richest honeycomb in disgust. On the other hand, someone who is genuinely starving finds even bitter food to be sweet and satisfying. In the same way, people satisfied with worldly pleasures ignore spiritual treasures, while those who sense their need welcome any truth from God.

A bird that wanders far from its nest leaves its home unprotected and puts its own life in danger. A person who aimlessly abandons his home, family duties, or God-given calling faces the same kind of trouble and distress. God calls people to stay faithful and settled in the places where He has placed them.

Rich ointments and sweet incense bring refreshment and delight to the senses. Even more pleasing is the heartfelt, sincere counsel that comes from a loyal friend. True friendship brings deep comfort by offering thoughtful advice to the soul.

Longstanding family friendships should be treasured and never cast aside. When trouble strikes, a dependable neighbor living right next door is often more helpful than a blood relative who lives far away. Proximity and proven loyalty make a nearby friend an immediate refuge in times of need.

A father pleads with his son to pursue wisdom and live an upright life. A son's good judgment brings deep joy to his parents and silences critics who accuse them of bad guidance. Believers who live wisely bring honor to their heavenly Father before those who mock the faith.

A prudent and sensible person notices danger ahead and takes shelter before trouble arrives. The simple, however, are naïve and careless, rushing forward into harm without thought and paying a heavy price. True wisdom pays attention to warnings and avoids unnecessary pitfalls.

If someone foolishly guarantees the debt of a stranger or an untrustworthy outsider, lenders should demand his cloak as security. A man who throws away his financial security on people he barely knows is irresponsible and untrustworthy. Sound judgment requires holding such reckless people accountable.

Shouting noisy blessings and overdone praise at a neighbor early in the morning sounds like self-serving flattery rather than genuine gratitude. Because the greeting is so loud, pushy, and poorly timed, listeners will treat it as an insincere curse designed to win favors. True thankfulness is quiet, humble, and considerate of others.

A quarrelsome person in a home is like a constant, irritating drip through a leaky roof during a heavy rainstorm. Trying to control or silence such an argumentative spouse is as impossible as grasping the wind or holding slippery oil in one's hand. Persistent strife at home wears away peace and cannot be hidden from view.

Just as one piece of hard iron or steel sharpens another through contact, people sharpen one another through honest conversation and companionship. Healthy interaction rubs away rough edges, stirs up the mind, and brightens a person's countenance. Godly friendships challenge and encourage believers to grow in wisdom and virtue.

A gardener who patiently tends a fig tree will eventually enjoy its sweet fruit in due season. In the same way, a servant who diligently cares for his master's interests will receive honor and reward for his loyalty. Faithful labor in any honest calling brings lasting benefits.

Just as calm water reflects the face of the person looking down into it, a person's heart reveals who he truly is. Looking into our inner motives, desires, and thoughts exposes our real spiritual character. We can also understand the struggles and nature of others by recognizing the same human heart within ourselves.

The realm of the dead and the place of destruction are never full, constantly swallowing up more lives. In the exact same way, human eyes and sinful cravings are never fully satisfied with worldly wealth, status, or pleasure. Only God can truly satisfy the deepest longings of the human soul.

A crucible tests the purity of silver and a hot furnace tests gold by melting away the dross. Similarly, a person's character is tested by how he responds to praise and popularity. Vain individuals become proud and conceited when commended, while wise individuals stay humble and give thanks to God.

Even if a stubborn fool were pounded in a mortar with a pestle like grain being crushed, his foolishness would still cling to him. Severe punishment and hard discipline cannot change someone whose heart is set on wickedness. Outward force alone cannot cure folly without God changing the inner heart.

A wise shepherd pays close attention to his sheep and carefully inspects the condition of his herds. Material wealth can quickly disappear, and even a royal crown does not automatically last forever without diligent care. Faithful stewardship of ordinary work provides a solid and enduring foundation for living.

When the harvest seasons roll by, the grass is cut, and wild herbs are gathered from the hills, God's creation provides for those who work hard. Lambs supply wool for warm clothing, goats provide income to purchase or rent land, and goats' milk provides plenty of wholesome food for the entire household. Honest, everyday labor under God's providence brings contentment and meets every basic need.
